title: Lovász Local Lemma OQ-01: The Symmetric Form of the Erdős–Lovász Induction Step
description: The induction-step entry (lovasz-local-lemma-oq-01-induction-step) verified the Erdős–Lovász step in its ASYMMETRIC shape: from a denominator lower bound d ≤ μ[⋂_{S₁} Aⱼᶜ | ⋂_{S₂} Aⱼᶜ] and the asymmetric budget μ(Aᵢ) ≤ x·d, the per-event failure over the full survival history stays ≤ x (cond_failure_le_x). There x and d are the per-event value xᵢ and the per-block product ∏_{j∈S₁}(1 − xⱼ), quantities that vary with the actual neighbour set S₁. The SYMMETRIC Lovász Local Lemma — the memorable textbook statement — instead assigns a single uniform value x to every event and bounds each event's dependency degree by a single constant d_max: Aᵢ depends on at most d_max others, and the numeric hypothesis is the uniform budget μ(Aᵢ) ≤ x·(1 − x)^{d_max} with the exponent the DEGREE BOUND, not the actual neighbour count |S₁|. This entry lands the bridge between the two forms. The key observation is a single ℝ≥0∞ order step: since the true neighbour block satisfies |S₁| ≤ d_max and in ℝ≥0∞ truncated subtraction gives 1 − x ≤ 1 UNCONDITIONALLY (tsub_le_self), the uniform product ∏_{j∈S₁}(1 − x) = (1 − x)^{|S₁|} is at least (1 − x)^{d_max} (fewer factors, each ≤ 1), i.e. (1 − x)^{d_max} ≤ ∏_{j∈S₁}(1 − x) with no x ≤ 1 hypothesis needed (one_sub_pow_le_prod_of_card_le). Hence the uniform budget μ(Aᵢ) ≤ x·(1 − x)^{d_max} implies the per-block budget μ(Aᵢ) ≤ x·∏_{j∈S₁}(1 − x) that the committed asymmetric invariant consumes (symmetric_budget_le), and threading it through cond_failure_le_x delivers the induction step in symmetric form: under |S₁| ≤ d, a denominator lower bound ∏_{S₁}(1 − x) ≤ μ[⋂_{S₁} Aⱼᶜ | ⋂_{S₂} Aⱼᶜ], and independence of Aᵢ from its non-neighbours, μ[Aᵢ | (⋂_{S₁} Aⱼᶜ) ∩ (⋂_{S₂} Aⱼᶜ)] ≤ x (cond_failure_le_x_symmetric). A closing lemma records that the optimal symmetric assignment x = (d+1)⁻¹ is admissible (x ≤ 1), at which the uniform budget x·(1 − x)^d = (d+1)⁻¹·(d/(d+1))^d is exactly the tight threshold T(d) of the gallery proof / euler-threshold entry, the value the classic symmetric LLL admits under e·p·(d+1) ≤ 1. Everything is over an arbitrary IsProbabilityMeasure; the denominator lower bound is left abstract exactly as in the induction-step entry. 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

originalContributions: one_sub_pow_le_prod_of_card_le: the degree-bound reduction. For a neighbour block S₁ with |S₁| ≤ d, (1 − x)^d ≤ ∏_{j∈S₁}(1 − x) in ℝ≥0∞, UNCONDITIONALLY (no x ≤ 1). The base 1 − x ≤ 1 holds by tsub_le_self (truncated subtraction), so pow_le_pow_of_le_one shrinks the power under the larger exponent d ≥ |S₁|; Finset.prod_const rewrites the product as (1 − x)^{|S₁|}. This is the single order step that lets the uniform (degree-bounded) LLL budget replace the per-block product budget — and its unconditional character (a genuine simplification over the naive '0 ≤ 1 − x ≤ 1' framing) is a small novelty of the ℝ≥0∞ setting.

symmetric_budget_le: the uniform budget implies the per-block budget. From μ(Aᵢ) ≤ x·(1 − x)^d (symmetric, exponent the degree bound) and |S₁| ≤ d, concludes μ(Aᵢ) ≤ x·∏_{j∈S₁}(1 − x) — the per-block asymmetric hypothesis consumed by InductionStep.cond_failure_le_x. cond_failure_le_x_symmetric: the Erdős–Lovász induction step in symmetric form. Under |S₁| ≤ d, a denominator lower bound ∏_{S₁}(1 − x) ≤ μ[⋂_{S₁} Aⱼᶜ | ⋂_{S₂} Aⱼᶜ] (nonzero), independence of Aᵢ from its non-neighbour block, and the UNIFORM degree-bounded budget μ(Aᵢ) ≤ x·(1 − x)^d, concludes μ[Aᵢ | (⋂_{S₁} Aⱼᶜ) ∩ (⋂_{S₂} Aⱼᶜ)] ≤ x. This is the symmetric-LLL form of the induction invariant — a single value x and a single degree bound d control every event, independent of the actual neighbour set — obtained by reducing the uniform budget to the per-block budget (symmetric_budget_le) and feeding it to the committed asymmetric invariant cond_failure_le_x with denominator ∏_{S₁}(1 − x).

symmetric_x_le_one: admissibility of the optimal symmetric assignment x = (d+1)⁻¹ (x ≤ 1, via ENNReal.inv_le_one and le_add_self), so cond_failure_le_x_symmetric applies to it. At this x the uniform budget x·(1 − x)^d = (d+1)⁻¹·(d/(d+1))^d is exactly the tight threshold T(d) maximizing x(1 − x)^d (lovasz-local-lemma-oq-01-euler-threshold), the value the classic symmetric LLL admits under e·p·(d+1) ≤ 1. Ties the ℝ≥0∞ symmetric step to the ℝ-valued threshold analysis.

Framing contribution: pins the exact algebraic gap between the asymmetric and symmetric measure-theoretic LLL. Every prior OQ-01 quantitative entry is stated per-block (product over the actual neighbour set); the textbook symmetric statement is per-degree (a single power of the degree bound). This entry shows the gap is a one-line ℝ≥0∞ monotonicity — antitonicity of b ↦ b^n at base b ≤ 1 — so the entire symmetric LLL reduces to the same denominator recursion plus this order step, with no new probability.

overview.historicalContext: The Lovász Local Lemma (Erdős–Lovász, 1975) has two standard shapes. The general ASYMMETRIC form assigns each bad event Aᵢ a real xᵢ ∈ (0,1) and requires Pr[Aᵢ] ≤ xᵢ·∏_{j ∈ Γ(i)}(1 − xⱼ), the product ranging over i's neighbours in the dependency graph; its conclusion is Pr[⋂ Āᵢ] ≥ ∏(1 − xᵢ) > 0. The memorable SYMMETRIC corollary — the version quoted in most applications — collapses this to a single degree bound d (each event depends on at most d others) and a single probability bound p, with the sufficient condition e·p·(d+1) ≤ 1 (equivalently p ≤ T(d) = dᵈ/(d+1)^{d+1}, the maximum of x(1 − x)^d attained at x = 1/(d+1)). The symmetric form is derived from the asymmetric one by taking every xᵢ = 1/(d+1) uniform and bounding the neighbour product ∏_{j ∈ Γ(i)}(1 − xⱼ) ≥ (1 − x)^d from below using |Γ(i)| ≤ d and 1 − x ≤ 1. The OQ-01 measure-theoretic gallery front had assembled the asymmetric induction step (the induction-step entry's cond_failure_le_x, in the shape μ(Aᵢ) ≤ x·d ⟹ μ[Aᵢ | history] ≤ x with d the per-block product) but stated everything per-block. This entry supplies the missing symmetric reduction: the same degree-bound monotonicity ∏_{Γ(i)}(1 − x) ≥ (1 − x)^d, over an ℝ≥0∞ probability measure, turning the asymmetric invariant into the symmetric one.
overview.problemStatement:
**Open question OQ-01 (from LovaszLocalLemma.lean)**: formalize the full probabilistic Lovász Local Lemma over measure-theoretic probability spaces, including the dependency-graph induction that produces per-event conditional bounds from a bounded dependency degree.

**This entry (symmetric form of the induction step)**: given the committed asymmetric induction-step invariant cond_failure_le_x (μ(Aᵢ) ≤ x·d ⟹ μ[Aᵢ | N ∩ C] ≤ x, N = neighbour survival, C = non-neighbour survival, d ≤ μ[N | C] a denominator lower bound), reduce the SYMMETRIC degree-bounded hypothesis μ(Aᵢ) ≤ x·(1 − x)^{d_max} (with |S₁| ≤ d_max) to the per-block hypothesis μ(Aᵢ) ≤ x·∏_{S₁}(1 − x), and thereby obtain the induction step's conclusion μ[Aᵢ | N ∩ C] ≤ x in the symmetric shape the classic LLL maintains.
overview.text: There are two ways to state the local lemma. The general one hands every bad event its own private budget and multiplies over exactly its neighbours; the famous one uses a single budget and a single bound on how many neighbours any event may have. The famous version is a corollary of the general one, and the bridge is a single inequality about numbers between zero and one: a product of factors each at most one only gets smaller when you add more factors, so a product over the real (bounded) neighbour set is at least the same factor raised to the worst-case degree. This entry formalizes that bridge inside the measure-theoretic development. It proves — with no assumption that the budget is itself below one, because in extended-nonnegative arithmetic one-minus-x never exceeds one for free — that the worst-case power lower-bounds the true product, hence the uniform budget implies the per-block budget the earlier entry already knew how to use, and the induction step goes through in its symmetric form. A short closing fact records that the textbook-optimal budget x = 1/(d+1) is a legitimate value here, connecting the step to the threshold the gallery's real-analysis entry pins down.
overview.proofStrategy:
**The reindexing (prod_const_one_sub).** Every factor of ∏_{j∈S₁}(1 − x) is the constant 1 − x, so Finset.prod_const gives ∏_{j∈S₁}(1 − x) = (1 − x)^{|S₁|}.

**The order step (one_sub_pow_le_prod_of_card_le).** In ℝ≥0∞, 1 − x ≤ 1 holds unconditionally (tsub_le_self: truncated subtraction never exceeds the minuend). With |S₁| ≤ d, pow_le_pow_of_le_one (zero_le _) tsub_le_self hcard gives (1 − x)^d ≤ (1 − x)^{|S₁|} = ∏_{j∈S₁}(1 − x). No x ≤ 1 hypothesis is required.

**The budget bridge (symmetric_budget_le).** Given p ≤ x·(1 − x)^d, gcongr reduces the target p ≤ x·∏_{S₁}(1 − x) to the order step (1 − x)^d ≤ ∏_{S₁}(1 − x), closed by one_sub_pow_le_prod_of_card_le.

**The symmetric invariant (cond_failure_le_x_symmetric).** Feed the per-block budget symmetric_budget_le hcard hlll : μ(Aᵢ) ≤ x·∏_{S₁}(1 − x) as the hlll argument of the committed InductionStep.cond_failure_le_x, with denominator d := ∏_{S₁}(1 − x), the given denominator lower bound hd, and hd0 ≠ 0. The conclusion μ[Aᵢ | N ∩ C] ≤ x is immediate.

**Admissibility (symmetric_x_le_one).** ENNReal.inv_le_one turns ((d : ℝ≥0∞) + 1)⁻¹ ≤ 1 into 1 ≤ d + 1, discharged by le_add_self.
keyInsights: The asymmetric–symmetric gap is a single ℝ≥0∞ monotonicity, not new probability. The whole measure-theoretic LLL scaffold was built per-block (products over the actual neighbour set), yet the textbook statement is per-degree (one power of the degree bound). This entry shows the difference is exactly the antitonicity of b ↦ bⁿ at base b ≤ 1: more factors, each ≤ 1, only shrink the product, so the worst-case power (1 − x)^d underestimates the true product ∏_{S₁}(1 − x). Everything else — the ratio, the numerator collapse, the denominator recursion — is shared between the two forms.

The reduction is unconditional in ℝ≥0∞. Over the reals one writes 0 ≤ 1 − x ≤ 1 and needs x ≤ 1 for the upper half. In ℝ≥0∞ truncated subtraction gives 1 − x ≤ 1 for FREE (tsub_le_self), with no constraint on x, so one_sub_pow_le_prod_of_card_le and the whole bridge hold for arbitrary x. The intended regime x ∈ [0,1] is recovered only where the budget x(1 − x)^d is meaningful; the inequality itself needs nothing.

The degree bound decouples the invariant from the neighbour set. cond_failure_le_x_symmetric controls μ[Aᵢ | history] ≤ x with a single x and a single d for every event, whatever its actual neighbours are — precisely the uniformity the symmetric LLL's strong induction relies on (the invariant must be stated with data independent of which subset S is being conditioned on).

The optimal budget lives at the euler-threshold entry's maximum. symmetric_x_le_one records that x = 1/(d+1) — the maximizer of x(1 − x)^d — is admissible, so the uniform budget x(1 − x)^d = T(d) is the tight threshold the real-analysis entry lovasz-local-lemma-oq-01-euler-threshold proves is implied by e·p·(d+1) ≤ 1. The ℝ≥0∞ induction machinery and the ℝ threshold analysis meet at this value.

sections.summary: Module docstring. Recalls the asymmetric induction-step invariant cond_failure_le_x (per-event value x, per-block denominator d = ∏_{S₁}(1 − xⱼ)) and contrasts it with the symmetric LLL's uniform budget μ(Aᵢ) ≤ x·(1 − x)^{d_max}, exponent the degree bound. conclusion.summary: The symmetric form of the Erdős–Lovász induction step is machine-verified over an arbitrary probability space: the degree-bound reduction (1 − x)^d ≤ ∏_{j∈S₁}(1 − x) for |S₁| ≤ d, unconditional in ℝ≥0∞ (one_sub_pow_le_prod_of_card_le); the budget bridge μ(Aᵢ) ≤ x·(1 − x)^d ⟹ μ(Aᵢ) ≤ x·∏_{S₁}(1 − x) (symmetric_budget_le); and the symmetric invariant μ[Aᵢ | (⋂_{S₁} Aⱼᶜ) ∩ (⋂_{S₂} Aⱼᶜ)] ≤ x from a uniform degree-bounded budget, a denominator lower bound, and non-neighbour independence (cond_failure_le_x_symmetric), with the optimal x = (d+1)⁻¹ shown admissible (symmetric_x_le_one). 0 sorries, 0 axioms.
conclusion.implications:
**Bridges the per-block asymmetric LLL machinery to the textbook symmetric statement.** Every prior OQ-01 quantitative entry works with products over the actual neighbour set; the memorable symmetric LLL uses a single power of the degree bound. This entry shows the gap is exactly the antitonicity of b ↦ bⁿ at base b ≤ 1 — a one-line ℝ≥0∞ monotonicity, unconditional in x — so the entire symmetric induction step follows from the committed asymmetric invariant with no new probability.

**Honest scope**: this is the symmetric reduction of the step, not the full LLL. The denominator lower bound ∏_{S₁}(1 − x) ≤ μ[⋂_{S₁} Aⱼᶜ | ⋂_{S₂} Aⱼᶜ] is an explicit hypothesis (the recursion producing it by iterating the denominator-step peel is the sibling denominator-recursion line of work), and the global strong induction assembling the per-event invariant into the avoidance conclusion μ(⋂ Aᵢᶜ) > 0 remains open. What this entry adds is that once the denominator recursion is in hand, the symmetric LLL — the form used in applications — follows from the same invariant via a single order step, and its optimal budget coincides with the euler-threshold entry's tight threshold T(d).
openQuestions: Assemble the global conclusion. This entry proves the per-event symmetric invariant μ[Aᵢ | survival history] ≤ x; the memorable statement is the positivity μ(⋂ᵢ Aᵢᶜ) > 0 (some assignment avoids every bad event). Formalize the telescoping/chain-rule step that multiplies the per-event bounds over all events to reach that positive-probability conclusion.

Derive the textbook threshold e·p·(d+1) ≤ 1 as a clean corollary. The uniform budget x(1 − x)^d is maximized at x = 1/(d+1) with value (1/(d+1))(d/(d+1))^d ≥ 1/(e(d+1)); hence p ≤ 1/(e(d+1)), equivalently e·p·(d+1) ≤ 1, suffices. Formalize (d/(d+1))^d ≥ 1/e (equivalently (1 + 1/d)^d ≤ e) to package the sufficient condition in its familiar form.

Bridge to the algorithmic (Moser–Tardos) LLL. The asymmetric→symmetric gap here is a single ℝ≥0∞ monotonicity on the measure-theoretic proof. Does the same uniform-x reduction transfer to the entropy-compression / resampling proof, yielding the constructive symmetric LLL with the same e·p·(d+1) ≤ 1 threshold?

Proves over ℝ that the memorable symmetric condition e·p·(d+1) ≤ 1 implies p ≤ T(d) = dᵈ/(d+1)^{d+1}, the maximum of x(1 − x)^d at x = 1/(d+1). symmetric_x_le_one records that this optimal x is admissible in cond_failure_le_x_symmetric, so the uniform budget x(1 − x)^d at that x is exactly T(d) — the point where the ℝ≥0∞ symmetric induction step and the ℝ threshold analysis meet.

Its single-neighbour survival peel is the engine of the recursion that produces the denominator lower bound ∏_{S₁}(1 − x) ≤ μ[⋂_{S₁} Aⱼᶜ | ⋂_{S₂} Aⱼᶜ] that cond_failure_le_x_symmetric takes as a hypothesis. In the uniform case the assembled bound is (1 − x)^{|S₁|}, which this entry lower-bounds by (1 − x)^{d_max}.

Gives the avoidance lower bound ∏(1 − bₖ) ≤ μ(⋂ Aᵢᶜ) from per-event failure bounds μ[A k | prefix] ≤ bₖ. The symmetric invariant proved here supplies bₖ = x uniform, the shape the symmetric LLL feeds into that avoidance bound to obtain (1 − x)ⁿ ≤ μ(⋂ Aᵢᶜ).
